prompt: Find the longest stretch of strictly increasing values in an int array. Complete longestRun so it returns {startIndex, length}, preferring the earliest start on ties.
explanation: Track the start of the run you are currently inside plus the best run seen so far. Whenever values[i] is not strictly greater than values[i - 1] the current run ends and a new one starts at i. Comparing with a strict > (rather than >=) keeps the best run from swallowing later ties, which is what makes the earliest start win.
hints: Keep two pieces of state: where the run you are currently in began, and the best {start, length} you have seen.
The current run breaks exactly when values[i] <= values[i - 1]; at that moment the next run starts at index i.
Update the best run only when the current length is strictly greater than the best length -- that is what makes ties keep the earlier start.
